set.st: An Englishman named Carr, returning from California in 1850, was poisoned while staying on a farm here and buried his gold nuggets and money before he died. Aug 1895: a man dragging a side hill in an orchard turned up a box of gold nuggets, quartz and a sack of flakes, reported as over $20,000 at the Ingham County Savings Bank. The story says Carr buried "this gold with other nuggets and money in this neighborhood". Pin is on the 1895 house mark, not the spot itself.
set.pl: Orchard farm on a side hill 4 mi E of Dimondale: a 40 on the 1895 Ingham County atlas (Delhi Twp), NE¼ NE¼ sec. 30 T3N R2W, house mark at the E edge of the forty on the 29/30 line road. 1874 atlas: no 1850-era owner confirmed on the plate.
set.n: The poisoned Englishman Carr's California gold, orchard farm east of Dimondale
pinev: Parcel-level: a full re-read of the 1895 Delhi plate puts the house mark at the E edge of the forty in NE¼ NE¼ sec. 30 T3N R2W, on the 29/30 line road (about 200 m). The 1874 Delhi plate does not confirm the 1850 farm-owner link.
